title: Baseline and Incremental: User, Item, and Request Debiasing in Instagram Feed Ranking
abstract: arXiv:2610.27423v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A feed ranker scores candidates with a value model, a weighted sum of engagement predictions. Each prediction conflates a baseline, what this viewer, item or request would produce anyway, with the incremental amount by which this candidate exceeds it. The literature mostly removes the baseline. We argue that a multi-signal value model should keep the raw prediction and add the incremental part as a separately weighted term. On Instagram Feed, three debiasing families deployed independently, for viewer habit, item popularity and request context, are one parameterised operator, and a design procedure picks a point in it. Media-type (format) bias goes instead to a debiased label chosen by the same procedure. In a controlled four-arm ablation of deployed Feed terms (neither term, each alone, both), the two-term arm beats both single-term arms at production weights on point estimates in 11 of 13 judged (term, metric) pairs. translated_title: 基线与增量：Instagram信息流排序中的用户、物品与请求去偏
translated_abstract: 信息流排序器使用价值模型为候选内容打分，该模型是各项互动预测的加权和。每个预测都混淆了两个部分：基线——即该观看者、该内容或该请求本来就会产生的互动量——以及该候选内容超出基线的增量部分。现有文献大多采取移除基线的做法。我们主张，多信号价值模型应当保留原始预测，并将增量部分作为一个单独加权的项加入模型。在Instagram信息流中，三个独立部署的去偏方案族（分别针对观看者习惯、内容热门度和请求上下文）实际上可统一为一个参数化算子，并通过一套设计流程在该算子中选取一个具体的点。媒体类型（格式）偏差则转而由同一流程所选定的去偏标签来处理。在一项针对已部署信息流项的受控四臂消融实验（无任何项、仅含其一、两者兼具）中，在生产权重下的点估计上，双项方案在13个受评判的（项，指标）对中有11个优于两个单项方案。在26个直接……
tldr: 该论文提出在Instagram信息流价值模型中同时保留原始预测（基线）并单独加权加入增量项，将观看者习惯、内容热门度和请求上下文三类独立部署的去偏统一为一个参数化算子，四臂消融实验证明基线加增量的双项设计在绝大多数指标上优于任何单项去偏方案。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes keeping the raw prediction (baseline) in Instagram Feed's value model while adding a separately weighted incremental term, unifying three independently deployed debiasing families—viewer habit, item popularity, and request context—into one parameterized operator, and a controlled four-arm ablation shows the two-term design beats either single term in 11 of 13 judged (term, metric) pairs.
